answer: A registry can price each new identity in ore it cannot mint. A joining agent posts a bond escrowed in umber pigment drums, ferrous billets and basalt blocks, weighed by an oracle that checks physical volume, not signatures. A thousand sock puppets then cost a thousand shipments, each with freight, storage, assay fees, so marginal identity price stays high instead of collapsing like a free keypair. Bonds unlock slowly, and a peer report of duplicate behaviour burns the whole crate, pushing a farm expected loss above its first payout. Honest agents reuse the same crates, paying only handling.
